title: W5: team agent configurations, the team tool scope and its guard, and deterministic Business, Data Science and fixture model-specialist agents delivered through the outbox
request: Build W5 of the approved collaborative workspace plan: every agent knows its tasks, the actions it may take, its responsibility and the report it owes; deterministic agents (no language model) on Policy and run() with a scripted client; team tools in a new registry scope with a guard over the action directory; the delivery target running the recipient agent, idempotent on the outbox row id.
spec: dclab_rnd/teamspace/agents.py (TeamAgentConfig built from team_work.DIRECTORY, job_description, the deterministic agents' rules, ScriptedChoices, run_turn, open_case, person_replies, correct, preview_report, deliver, install); dclab_rnd/teamspace/tools.py (scope team: accept, block, clarify, record_human_response, answer, delegate, act, model_call, return_report; TeamGuard); dclab_rnd/teamspace/fixtures.py (invented renewal samples, ETA E1 and acceptance A1); registry scope team, GROUPS team, harness.AGENTS teamspace; tests/test_teamspace_agents.py on files and PostgreSQL.
plan: read the plan's core design and W5, the owner's action directory, walkthroughs and report fields
read W1 team_work (DIRECTORY, may_take, can_claim, build_report, next_owner, may_approve), the W4 store and delivery, W2 teams, the agent runtime, registry and harness gates
derive each configuration from the directory and bind every action to a team-scope tool or a recorded human answer
write the guard: directory, binding, forbidden actions, the person behind a human answer, task ownership, authority at tool execution
write the agents as rules over the stored task so a repeated delivery finds nothing left
test the renewal round trip, the blocker, the two branches in both orders, a denied specialist, the kitchen correction and duplicate delivery on files and PostgreSQL
run the harness, prompt and harness-suite gates and the registry tests

decisions.decision: The deterministic agents choose each call from the task as stored, not from the row that woke them.
decisions.why: a delivery handed over twice (a crash after the agent acted, before the row was marked delivered) then finds its work done and runs no step, and a turn cut off midway resumes where it stopped; per-row markers would skip the rest of a half-done turn

decisions.decision: Business records its own actions on the task it requested, not on a task of its own.
decisions.why: a Business-owned task would put a Business to Business row in the shared handoff history; on the requested task the history reads exactly as the owner's example and the Business thread gets one reply

decisions.decision: Task moves (accept, block, complete through return_report) record no directory action; work actions do.
decisions.why: the directory lists work (inspect, confirm, delegate, score), not status changes; validate_transition already checks who moves a task

decisions.decision: Actions are written running and then finished, with an action id derived from the retry key.
decisions.why: the W4 store has no update from planned to running (a second record is refused); a derived id makes a retried call find its record

decisions.decision: The outbox's default target posts the row into its team thread (W3) and then gives the recipient agent its turn (W5).
decisions.why: no start-up call is needed; both halves are idempotent on the row id (the post keyed delivery:<id>, the agent reading the stored task)

decisions.decision: The answer to a clarification is a public store call, send_answer, on files and PostgreSQL.
decisions.why: the store only wrote an answer row when the owner moved its task, which would make Business act as Data Science; private store methods from another module would break silently

decisions.decision: The team agents' Policy carries chooser rules, and the ledger records their tool choices and stops as rule:teamspace.<agent>.
decisions.why: code chose those steps; recording them as model_role would label rules as a model's decisions in the training data

change: dclab_rnd/teamspace/agents.py, tools.py, fixtures.py (new); dclab_rnd/agents/registry.py (scope team); dclab_rnd/agents/__init__.py (GROUPS team); dclab_rnd/agents/harness.py (AGENTS teamspace); tests/test_teamspace_agents.py (new); tests/test_agent_harness.py (its probe); tests/test_agents_runtime.py and tests/test_agents_validator.py (the team scope's moves). Wiring after W3: teamspace/delivery.py default_target composes threads.deliver and agents.deliver; teamspace/store.py send_answer and storage TeamWork Protocol; ledger/capture.py records rules-chosen agent steps as rules; tests/test_teamspace_threads.py pins its delivery suite to the thread post alone. Joint review: store.report_task and delegate(parent_waits), store.reply_text, threads and team work in storage migrate, delivery lanes (lane_of), the SSE recheck on the live role, the post route handing a message to the thread's agent (TeamMessagePost.ask, api.js regenerated), tests/test_teamspace_routes.py.

findings.defect: Data Science opened only the first of the two specialist tasks for the food delivery question.
findings.scenario: the dispatch question needs ETA and acceptance; after the first delegation the parent moved to waiting_for_team and the rules only delegated from accepted, so the acceptance child never existed
findings.cause: the delegation branch was guarded by the accepted status that the delegation itself changes
findings.fix: delegate every missing specialist while the task is accepted or waiting_for_team

findings.defect: The preview of a finished task's report was forced to partial.
findings.scenario: a complete parent previewed after both children returned would read partial
findings.cause: the preview passed status partial for every unblocked task
findings.fix: partial only while a child is still out; otherwise the status build_report derives

findings.defect: Authority was rechecked at delivery but not when a team tool ran.
findings.scenario: sara is removed from the workspace after her case is delivered; person_replies in her name would still record a response and send an answer
findings.cause: the guard checked the directory and the task but not the member the turn acts for
findings.fix: the guard rechecks the initiating member through delivery.authorize before every team tool

findings.defect: The registry tests enumerate every scope's moves and failed on the new team scope.
findings.scenario: test_agents_runtime and test_agents_validator raised KeyError team
findings.cause: a new scope needs its moves in the tests' scope-to-moves maps
findings.fix: tools.MOVES lists the team scope's moves and both tests read it

findings.defect: An agent could record a person's answer that the person never gave.
findings.scenario: person_replies(person='sara', initiator=omar) recorded confirm_terms as answered by sara; a direct team_record_human_response with responded_by='sara' in omar's turn did the same
findings.cause: responded_by came from the tool's arguments and was checked only against the case member
findings.fix: the guard requires responded_by to be the turn's member and person, and the owner's relayed record needs the requester's finished record of the same response and person

findings.defect: A crash between the move to complete and the report left a task complete with no report, never reported again.
findings.scenario: the worker dies after move(complete), before store_report: the next turn sees complete and does nothing
findings.cause: two store writes in sequence, and rules that did not resume a complete task without a report
findings.fix: store.report_task moves and reports in one transaction (files and PostgreSQL); the rules report again for a complete task without a report; delegate moves the parent in the child's transaction

findings.defect: Two Data Science turns on one parent raced, and the loser's row was blocked.
findings.scenario: both branch replies delivered at once by two jobs: the second turn's move to complete fails with 'already complete' and becomes a PermanentFailure
findings.cause: one delivery job per child task, and a refusal for a move already made
findings.fix: a child's reply travels in its parent's lane (one job); the report is a duplicate when another turn stored the same revision; a move to the status the task already has is the same move

findings.defect: Fixture results were not labelled as simulated in threads or the handoff history.
findings.scenario: the dispatch brief read 'At 18:00 the estimated arrival was 18:32...' in the Business thread with no sign it came from fixtures
findings.cause: the reply text was the bare answer
findings.fix: the reply's first line says 'Simulated (fixture E1/A1):' whenever the report is simulated; the history shows that first line

findings.defect: Data Science's checks on an invented sample were recorded as real successes.
findings.scenario: inspect_schema, check_leakage, define_baseline and explain_uncertainty on sample:renewal_v1 were succeeded and the report not simulated
findings.cause: the act tool did not know its input was a fixture
findings.fix: checks on a fixtures.SAMPLES table are recorded simulated, so the report is simulated

findings.defect: Two signed-in people finishing steps 1-4 through the routes was not proven.
findings.scenario: a person's answer posted in their thread never reached the agent
findings.cause: the post route only saved the message
findings.fix: the post route hands the message to the thread's agent (ask opens a case; an answer to an open question is the person's answer); Sara and Dan finish the case through the routes with sign-in on

findings.defect: A Business member could not read the four questions from the thread alone.
findings.scenario: the reply message carried only the answer
findings.cause: no reply text beyond the answer
findings.fix: each reply says what was found, Why (evidence and a limit), Next (owner and what unblocks it) and Changed (the report it replaces and the current one)

measurements.name: team agents tests on files and on PostgreSQL, and the agent gates
measurements.gate: test_teamspace_agents passes on files and with --pg with no skipped test; test_agent_harness, test_prompt_gate, test_harness_gate, test_agents_runtime, test_agents_validator, test_harness_stage2, test_mcp, test_teamspace_store and test_teamspace_delivery still pass
measurements.result: after the joint review: test_teamspace_agents 31 and test_teamspace_routes 7 pass on files and --pg (the signed-in route test and the migrate test on PostgreSQL), with W2, W3, W4 and storage tests, the harness, prompt and harness-suite gates, registry, web client and decision capture tests
measurements.next: W6: corrections through bases and stale marking; wire install() (or delivery's default target) once W3 lands
limits: no language model is involved; every choice is code's
the samples and model results are invented fixtures; the specialists' results are labelled simulated
make check-quick and make check-all were not run in this package

outcome: Every directory row has a configuration and a job description built from the directory itself. The team scope's tools record each action through the W4 store behind a guard over the directory, the binding, forbidden actions, the person behind a human answer and the member's authority. Deterministic Business, Data Science and fixture model-specialist agents carry the renewal round trip, the blocker, the two-branch food delivery, a denied specialist and the kitchen correction through the outbox, and a repeated delivery runs no step.
lessons: Rules that read the stored state make a delivery target idempotent and resumable at once; a per-row marker gives only the first.
A move that a step makes (accepted to waiting_for_team) can close the branch that should run next; test the second delegation, not only the first.
risks: W3's delivery tests now pin the target to threads.deliver; any test that relies on the default target alone will see the agents act.
make sft-dev must run with the commit (test_devlog is stale until then).
